newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end higher but gains pared late.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end higher but gains pared late.

text.p: CME lumber futures ran up the expanded daily limit of $15.00 in May and posted new contract highs in May through September on rising cash lumber prices before gains were trimmed late on profit taking, traders said.

Lumber ended $9.90 per thousand board feet higher to $11.50 lower with only distant January off. May paced the advance at $411.50 and July ended up $5.40 at $402.80. May set a high of $416.60, July at $409.00 and September at $397.80.
Carryover buy stops from two days of limit gains and further demand prompted by climbing cash prices lifted futures from the start, traders said.
"Cash is very strong - wood is very tight," said Roger Champagne, marketing manager for Capital Forest Products Inc.

Champagne said much of the strength in cash came from the industry being short of wood going into the spring demand season. Buyers were waiting for heavy shipments of wood from Canada at the start of the new quota year, but those shipments never materialized.

"A lot of people were under the assumption that there was going to be this wall of wood to come down from Canada after the first (of the month) because of the quota, but it's just not there," Champagne said.

With warmer weather ahead the prospect is for cash prices to go even higher. Traders cited reports of cash lumber trading in the $405 to $415 range, up from the last official quote Wednesday of $394. Some Canadian mills have stopped taking orders after building order files out three weeks and increased demand in Canada for wood was adding to cash strength.

"Canadian government's made some monetary moves which made interest rates very desirable - housing starts are going to be very strong there for a couple of years. And the Canadian side has consumed more lumber than people thought," Champagne added.
